title: How Walking Through Doorways Wipes Your Memory

acts.name: Cold_Open_Sensory_Test
sentences: Stand up to grab kitchen scissors right now, and watch the doorway wipe your mind!
To test why, Notre Dame doctors had folks carry closed shoeboxes from table to table.
Each person tucked a red block inside their box and shut the lid.

acts.name: Notepad_Myth_To_Doorframe
sentences: For years, textbooks said five seconds of walking can't touch a fresh memory.
Yet walking through a doorway shifts the walls and wakes your map of space.
Then your brain's memory hub, the hippocampus, fires boundary cells to save that room.

acts.name: Prefrontal_Flush_And_Error_Jump
sentences: That pulse clears the spot behind your forehead, the prefrontal cortex, wiping your goal.
Walking through a doorway jumped box errors from twenty-three percent up to twenty-eight percent.

acts.name: Same_Room_Vs_Doorway_Control
sentences: Wait, what if walking across the floor, not the doorframe, made those blocks fade?
So folks walked the exact same distance across one room or through an open doorway.
Staying in one room kept memory sharp, showing the doorframe triggers the wipe.

acts.name: Boundary_Cells_And_Multitasking
sentences: That's because boundary cells treat each doorway like a clean cut between scenes.
Worse yet, holding two tasks in mind leaves zero grip at the door.

acts.name: Return_Room_Twist_And_Hand_Cue
sentences: Wait, what if you walk straight back into that first room to bring your lost memory back?
In fact, walking back through a second doorway fired one more reset instead.
Carry one clue in hand or say one word out loud before any door.

viewer_description:
At the University of Notre Dame, psychologists asked volunteers to carry colored wooden blocks inside closed shoeboxes from table to table. Walking across one large room caused a twenty-three percent memory error rate, while walking the exact same distance through an open doorway raised errors to twenty-eight percent.

Brain scans and single-neuron recordings show that crossing a doorway fires boundary cells in the hippocampus to archive the last room while clearing the front working-memory desk. Walking back through a second doorway triggered another reset instead of restoring recall.

Research: Radvansky, Krawietz and Tamplin, University of Notre Dame (2011), Baldassano et al. (2017), and Zheng et al. (2022).
debate_question: When you blank in the kitchen doorway, do you retrace your steps or stand still until it clicks?
